entries.mem0ai/mem0: Mem0 is a universal memory layer for AI agents and an official Hermes Agent memory provider, available as managed cloud or self-hosted open-source software. It supports semantic, keyword, and entity-based retrieval, with SDKs, a CLI, and a self-hosted server.
entries.vectorize-io/hindsight: Hindsight structures agent memory around retain, recall, and reflect operations. It supports hosted and local LLM providers, with deployment options including Docker, pip, and Kubernetes.
entries.volcengine/OpenViking: OpenViking is an open-source context database and official Hermes Agent memory provider that organizes resources, memories, and skills as files. It supports scoped semantic search across directories and archives sessions into inspectable Markdown memories.
entries.topoteretes/cognee: Cognee is an open-source memory platform that gives agents persistent memory across sessions using a self-hosted knowledge graph engine. It structures text into entities, relationships, and searchable chunks, and supports custom data models, plugins, and MCP.
entries.supermemoryai/supermemory: Supermemory is a memory engine and API, and an official Hermes Agent memory provider, that extracts conversation facts, handles contradictions, and manages automatic forgetting. It also connects to services including Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, OneDrive, and GitHub, and processes PDFs, images, videos, and code.
entries.garrytan/gbrain: Gbrain is an opinionated brain for OpenClaw and Hermes Agent that stores facts with provenance and supports correcting or withdrawing them. It can share memory across agents while keeping transient task state local; semantic search, synthesis, and background enrichment are optional.
entries.plastic-labs/honcho: Honcho is a memory library for building stateful agents and the upstream library used by the elkimek/honcho-self-hosted Hermes wrapper. It tracks peers across workspaces and sessions, offers Python and TypeScript SDKs, and can run locally or be self-hosted.
entries.campfirein/byterover-cli: ByteRover CLI treats memory as a Git-managed repository, with version control for a context tree through commit, branch, and merge commands. It is an official Hermes Agent memory provider with a five-tier retrieval system, an interactive TUI and REPL, and support for 20 LLM providers.
entries.mnemosyne-oss/mnemosyne: Mnemosyne is a SQLite-backed memory layer for Hermes agents with one pure-Python dependency. It can integrate through MCP, native providers, or a Python SDK; its README reports BEAM results for v3.0.0 and marks LongMemEval as pending.
entries.moorcheh-ai/memanto: Memanto extracts and consolidates memories across agents, reconciles conflicting information, and manages forgetting. It also supports exchanging memories through the Open Knowledge Format.
entries.ClaudioDrews/memory-os: Memory OS is a seven-layer memory system for Hermes Agent that includes vector search, structured facts, fabric recall, and an auto-curated wiki. It uses local infrastructure with Docker, Qdrant, Redis, and SQLite, and applies a Ground Truth hierarchy to prioritize injected context.
entries.greyhaven-ai/autocontext: AutoContext is a recursive self-improving context harness that helps agents tackle complex tasks by running them against evaluations. It keeps useful lessons, discards dead ends, and produces traces, reports, and playbooks.
entries.stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm: This Hermes Agent plugin uses a SQLite store and hierarchical DAG to persist messages. Its lcm_grep and lcm_recall tools help recover details from that stored context.
entries.vshulcz/deja-vu: Deja-vu searches session histories across supported coding agents, helping users find past work and resume a session or continue it in another agent. Semantic recall is optional, and it runs without a model or server by default.
entries.elkimek/honcho-self-hosted: This project provides a self-hosted Honcho backend for private, cross-session memory in Hermes Agent. It supports OpenAI-compatible providers and local inference servers, with an automated setup script for Docker, PostgreSQL, and Redis.
entries.Signet-AI/signetai: Signet provides a local-first layer for agent identity, memory, and secrets, with portable state across several agent harnesses and MCP clients. It connects through hooks, plugins, or extensions and includes a dashboard for browsing memory and asking questions.
entries.plur-ai/plur: Plur stores shared agent memories as plain YAML files in an open engram format. It offers local search with keyword search as a fallback, plus a CLI and MCP server.
entries.yoloshii/ClawMem: ClawMem is an on-device memory and context engine that combines BM25, vector search, rank fusion, and cross-encoder reranking. It can generate session handoffs and capture decisions and preferences, with integrations through hooks, MCP, and native agent plugins.
entries.Sibyl-Labs/Sibyl-Memory: Sibyl-Memory stores long-term memory locally in a SQLite file, using FTS5 search and a five-tier schema without a vector database or embeddings. Its package family includes an SDK, CLI, Hermes adapter, MCP server, and LangGraph BaseStore.
entries.EfficientContext/ContextPilot: ContextPilot optimizes context ordering, deduplication, and cache-aware scheduling, including text and multimodal reordering for prefix-cache sharing. It integrates with Hermes Agent, vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, and OpenClaw.
entries.yantrikos/yantrikdb-hermes-plugin: This Hermes memory plugin provides explainable retrieval: each recall result includes a why_retrieved reason. It also supports memory canonicalization and contradiction tracking, with an embedded backend by default and an HTTP option.
entries.ccf/agentcairn: AgentCairn provides long-term, cross-project memory for coding agents, keeping durable memories as inspectable Markdown files in an Obsidian vault. A local DuckDB cache supports hybrid search and retrieval, while MCP servers and host-specific plugins connect it to agents.
entries.JanYork/llm-wiki-cli: This agent-driven memory CLI maintains a source-grounded Wiki with citations and history across sessions. It is designed to recall, maintain, and evolve knowledge without embeddings or a vector database.
entries.amanning3390/flowstate-qmd: Flowstate-qmd uses an anticipatory cache that watches agent session logs to prefetch context. It combines local SQLite-vec storage with GGUF models via node-llama-cpp and provides an MCP-native server with automated configuration for major coding-agent clients.
entries.yepyhun/Brainstack: Brainstack combines Hindsight, Graphiti, and MemPalace under a single memory owner, using SQLite, Kuzu, and Chroma for state and retrieval. It provides the agent with a purpose-built evidence packet for each query.
entries.generalbusiness-ai/keep: Keep combines semantic search with BM25 full-text search and ranked graph traversal, while indexing codebases, URLs, and multimedia with OCR support. Its edge tags link stored notes through navigable, bidirectional relationships.
entries.aliasocracy/hermes-tool-slimmer: Hermes Tool Slimmer reduces tool-schema tokens through local keyword-based ranking and supports Tool Search. It integrates as middleware without patching Hermes core on version 0.19 or later, and includes a dashboard for monitoring savings and managing tool configurations.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-context-os: Agent Context OS provides a Git-backed context and workflow layer for Claude Code, Codex, and other listed compatible agents. Its workflows cover migrations, handoffs, and memory proposals, with integrations that are opt-in rather than enabled automatically.
entries.Ladybug-Memory/hermes-memory-plugin: This local-only Hermes plugin stores memory in a single .lbdb embedded graph database file and supports BM25 keyword search with named relationships between entries. Importance-weighted recall prioritizes high-importance memories during context prefetch.
entries.stepanov1975/hermes-local-knowledge: Hermes Local Knowledge indexes configured local sources and selected Hermes runtime sources, then registers five tools for search, retrieval, traversal, feedback, and usage reports. It also registers hooks for pre-LLM calls and session end and finalization.
entries.MukundaKatta/hermes-agentmemory: Hermes AgentMemory is a pull-model episodic memory plugin with an on-demand summarizer and a trace.jsonl audit log of prefetch operations. It supports immediate event deletion rather than retaining deleted events in persistent summaries.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/hermes-blind: Hermes Blind recovers the original goal from the first user turn of a long Claude Code or Codex session, with goals, first-sentence, and full extraction modes. It skips tool output and other non-user-turn records, and does not use a summarizing model or external service.
entries.piprail/piprail: Piprail provides a TypeScript SDK for x402 payments and an MCP server for budget-bound agent wallets. It operates without a backend, database, or API keys.
entries.yonro/hermes-xmemo-plugin: The XMemo plugin runs inside Hermes and communicates with XMemo over HTTPS to provide durable, cross-session memory with semantic search. It offers ranked, bounded context recall before a turn and includes a local SQLite reliability layer.
entries.futurebrowser/hermes-exabase-plugin: The Exabase plugin integrates Exabase M-1 for self-organizing long-term agent memory. It provides tools to search and manually store memories, with configurable query expansion and result reranking for retrieval.
entries.sourcevault-ai/sourcevault-code-tools: SourceVault Code Tools provides private local code memory for repositories, with slash commands for search, file reads, context, and Q&A. It supports Hermes CLI, Telegram, and Hermes Desktop, and includes repo sync and indexed git-history search commands.
entries.visorcraft/MongrelDB-Hermes: MongrelDB-Hermes provides long-term memory for Hermes Agent, with AES-256-GCM encryption at rest enabled by default. It offers retrieval using HNSW ANN, sparse search, and an FM-index, and can run through native Rust FFI or an HTTP daemon.
entries.penfieldlabs/hermes-penfield: Penfield provides memory-management and knowledge-graph traversal tools for Hermes Agent. Its hybrid search combines BM25, vector, and graph methods, and it can automatically checkpoint context during message compression.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-memory-kit: Agent Memory Kit curates agent memory stored in plain Markdown files, producing JSON diffs for review rather than using a database. Its “rot” and “lint” curators identify stale or conflicting facts, while a local Git repository tracks and lets you revert changes.

entries.obra/superpowers: Superpowers is an agentic skills framework paired with a software-development workflow that covers specification, planning, and subagent-driven development. Its skills trigger automatically in supported coding-agent harnesses, and the README provides installation instructions for multiple coding agents.
entries.nexu-io/open-design: Open Design is a local-first system for creating and refining interactive web prototypes with a live preview, as well as slide decks, images, and motion graphics. It includes skills, design templates, design systems, and plugins, and supports coding-agent CLIs including Hermes Agent.
entries.mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills: This project provides structured cybersecurity skills across 34 security domains, with mappings to MITRE ATT&CK, ATLAS, D3FEND, and F3 frameworks. Its README says the skills are compatible with more than 26 AI platforms.
entries.Agents365-ai/drawio-skill: Drawio-skill turns natural-language prompts and real sources into editable .drawio diagrams. Its incremental sync preserves manual layout and annotations, and it offers the diagramctl CLI with an optional MCP server.
entries.internet-court/internet-court-skill: Internet Court provides a master router and connector skills for agent-to-agent commerce, alongside vendored copies of official protocol skills. It also adds verification and dispute resolution.
entries.conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing: Avoid AI Writing audits files or piped text for detectable AI-writing patterns and can score the content. Its rewrite mode supports up to two editing passes, while in-place editing refuses source code, configuration, and generated data.
entries.AMAP-ML/SkillClaw: SkillClaw unifies skills across agents and devices, with integrations including Hermes, Codex, and Claude Code. Its dashboard covers skills, validation, versions, and session traces.
entries.wondelai/skills: This cross-platform skills library includes 51 expert frameworks and 14 guided metaskills, and supports Claude Code, Codex, and agent-plugins.org specifications. It also maintains session state in the project's docs folder.
entries.mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills: This collection offers 822 professional agent skills that run natively in Hermes Agent and Claude Code, with ready-to-paste exports for other assistants. Skills include frameworks, output templates, quality checks, and anti-patterns; the README gives an installation command and identifies the project as MIT-licensed.
entries.ZeroPointRepo/youtube-skills: YouTube-skills provides skills for transcripts, video search, channel browsing, and playlist extraction, and is compatible with Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Claude Code, and Cursor. It requires a TranscriptAPI key, which the README says has a 100-credit free tier.
entries.Romanescu11/hermes-skill-factory: Hermes Skill Factory watches active workflows to detect and propose reusable skills, then generates both SKILL.md documentation and Python plugin scaffolds. Slash commands let users manage, list, and save detected patterns.
entries.Cranot/super-hermes: Super-Hermes helps Hermes Agent generate custom thinking instructions for specific tasks and includes pre-built analytical lenses for various domains. It reports findings alongside a report of analysis blind spots.
entries.DougTrajano/pydantic-ai-skills: Adds type-safe agentskills.io support to Pydantic AI, with progressive disclosure and remote skill registries from Git and S3. It also provides tools for bundled resources and script execution, including sandboxing to isolate untrusted scripts from the host.
entries.tlehman/litprog-skill: Creates literate programming documents that combine prose, diagrams, and source code in `.lit.md` files, then extracts runnable source files from them. When source files change, it syncs those edits back to the literate document, making it useful for keeping agent-facing explanations and code aligned.
entries.AkoliteZA/hermes-agent-idea-workflow: Turns rough ideas into structured design documents and implementation handoffs for Hermes Agent. Lite and Full modes accommodate different levels of project complexity, while a spec review gate evaluates work as PASS or FAIL.
entries.ReinaMacCredy/maestro: Maestro is a harness for long-running AI agents, with structured memory, cross-feature learning, and a plan-approve-execute approach. It requires no background service and includes an SLP protocol for supervised teams, plus CLI commands for installation, updates, and diagnostics.
entries.esaradev/icarus-plugin: Icarus provides cross-instance shared memory through Markdown files and automatically captures high-value decisions and outcomes. It also includes a pipeline for fine-tuning and switching to replacement models, pairing memory of past work with a way to train a successor.
entries.Hermes-brasil/hermes-brasil: This Portuguese-language Hermes Agent community project offers skills in SKILL.md format and guides covering installation, production, cron, MCP, and skill authoring. Contributions are submitted through pull requests, making it a community resource for Portuguese-speaking users and contributors.
entries.black-forest-labs/skills: Black Forest Labs’ skills focus on prompting for FLUX image and video generation, with BFL API integration for polling and webhooks. The collection also includes a FLUX 3 video suite with eight specialist skills.
entries.smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills: This repository lists nine Chainlink skills, each following the Agent Skills specification, and can be installed with `npx skills add smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills`. The README describes the repository as containing community examples only.
entries.armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge: Skill Forge creates agent instructions from repositories, documentation, and developer discourse, with both automated and step-by-step workflows. It also supports skill testing and export, covering the process from source material to a finished skill.
entries.supernovae-st/nika: Nika is a workflow language for AI that checks workflows before calling a model and lets users choose the model. It also verifies each run’s tamper-evident record, making run verification part of the workflow.
entries.chigwell/skilldock.io: Skilldock is a registry of reusable AI skills based on the AgentSkills specification, with both a Python client and a CLI. Its installation flow resolves dependencies recursively, and it includes commerce features using TON payments.
entries.tiann/execplan-skill: Execplan supports autonomous execution of long-running, multi-step tasks with checkpoints and real-time tracking of progress and decisions. Built-in rollback procedures provide a recovery path when execution needs to be reversed.
entries.adnw-vinc/hermes-nextcloud: This Hermes Agent skill manages Nextcloud files, notes, calendars, tasks, and contacts using WebDAV and CalDAV. It uses HTTPS with Nextcloud App Passwords and includes a guided setup script for validating credentials and configuring access.
entries.amanning3390/hermeshub: HermesHub is a community hub for browsing, searching, and installing skills, with federated search across GitHub and Hugging Face. It implements the Agentic Resource Discovery v0.9 specification and operates autonomously via Hermes Agent on NVIDIA infrastructure.
entries.willingning-coder/eagle-eye: Eagle Eye retrieves relevant skills through five layers, from hard triggers to semantic embeddings, with results combined using RRF fusion. By narrowing the skill list before LLM calls, it aims to reduce token use, and it can degrade gracefully when embedding models or dependencies are unavailable.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermaguard: Hermaguard is a read-only code-review skill that uses parallel subagents to examine edge cases, adversarial risks, and integration issues, then consolidates and triages findings. It pairs deterministic scans with proof-of-concept execution in a hardened sandbox to verify findings rather than fix code.
entries.EntangledQuantum/Life_OS: Life_OS is a personal execution system for habits, study blocks, and other tasks, with daily habit scoring. It runs locally with SQLite storage, includes an Android client, and connects to agents over MCP.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermes-simplify-swarm: This skill simplifies code through three parallel agents focused on Hygiene, Clarity, and Correctness. It supports TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, and Rust, and applies changes through risk tiers with an approval gate.
entries.handnewb/hermes-cybersec-lab: Hermes Cybersec Lab provides a cybersecurity skill and tool collection, with the highlights listing 2,077 skills across repositories and 131+ tools for networking, forensics, and exploitation. It also integrates 28 cybersecurity frameworks and standards, including MITRE ATT&CK, MISP, CVSS, and OWASP.
entries.teixeirazeus/fablize-for-hermes: Fablize for Hermes adapts verified procedures for task decomposition, requiring evidence-based verification gates across multiple stories. It also provides an investigation protocol for reproduction and causal debugging, plus a Python goal engine for persistent task state.
entries.PederHP/skillsdotnet: Skillsdotnet implements agentskills.io in C#/.NET, using SKILL.md files for progressive disclosure. It integrates with Microsoft.Extensions.AI for tool-based skill loading and can automatically register common agent skill directories.
entries.Diabloluo/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is a local, real-time observability dashboard for token costs, session history, and skill analytics, alongside timelines, health, cron, channels, and incidents. It uses read-only local data access with log desensitization and offers optional incident alerts through Telegram and Feishu.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skills: This collection offers plain-markdown skills for code review, session management, multi-session reconciliation, worktree recovery, and skill scaffolding across several coding agents. Skills can be installed by copying a directory or using the bundled installer.
entries.conorbronsdon/demo-gif-skill: Creates reproducible VHS tape or Playwright recording scripts to add demo GIFs to repository READMEs, with support for terminal CLIs, TUIs, web apps, and libraries. It also optimizes GIFs toward a target size under 8 MB, making it a practical skill for producing compact, repeatable project demos.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skill-builder: Builds Claude Code extensions and portable Agent Skills core files, then validates them against runtime-specific profiles with CI-friendly exit codes. It also checks official frontmatter specifications weekly for field drift, setting it apart as a skill focused on keeping other skills current.
entries.aidevelopers2/remoteopenclaw-mcp: Lets a terminal or AI agent search more than 13,870 MCP servers and 4,384 agent skills, and provides direct installation commands for discovered tools and plugins. Its MCP-compatible client integrations include Hermes, Cursor, and Claude Code.
entries.Carlo1911/skill-evolution: Analyzes past sessions and indexes installed skills to draft structured improvement proposals for agent skills. Proposals are review-only by default, with automatic application gated by deterministic, LLM-judge, or regression evaluators.
entries.superagnt/leverage: Provides agent skills for social data, web research, and enrichment, alongside packaged skills that combine an agent, skills, and a data flow. It also invites community contributions in `skills/community/`.
entries.CorsenAI/hermes-windows-runtime-skills: Provides Hermes Agent skills for routing file operations with environment-specific path syntax and selecting and verifying existing, project-compatible Python interpreters. It supports native Windows, Git Bash/MSYS, and WSL environments.
entries.jiawood2006/hermes-skills: Offers Hermes skills for transcribing Douyin videos into structured Markdown and SRT subtitles, removing common Chinese AI-writing patterns with a rule-based engine, and extracting structured data from PDFs and images using macOS Vision. The collection also includes an e-commerce materials studio.
entries.webmilmind1/hermes-bounty-board: Lets agents list open support bounties, purchase ticket context, and submit answers for human review, with public wallet earnings records. Board creation returns a URL, API key, and USDC deposit addresses.
entries.mag3nt-com/openclaw-skill: Automates USDC payments for HTTP 402 responses and supports Pay Link, x402, MPP, and AP2 protocols. It is compatible with OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and the agentskills.io standard.
entries.skillseal/skillseal: Tests agent skills for structure, functionality, and security in isolated Docker containers. It produces Ed25519-signed certificates and provides a public API for certificate verification and skill submission.
entries.scavio-ai/hermes-agent: Provides structured web data across 31 platforms through a hosted MCP server exposing 191 tools, plus five ready-to-use workflow skills. It also supports Claude, Cursor, Goose, and OpenHands.
entries.parkyucheol-del/alphapipeline: Provides token honeypot, tax, and liquidity risk checks, along with market data that includes DEX slippage and funding rates. Agents can access it through REST endpoints or a remote MCP server.
entries.NickSF189/kisscode-agent: This skill helps AI agents join KissCode, with a one-call registration example and SKILL.md and HEARTBEAT.md files. It also lists installation options for several agent platforms and includes a README badge snippet.
entries.Shine8592/china-briefing: This Hermes Agent skill generates structured Chinese news briefings across geographic scales, from global to street level. Reports include core conclusions and action suggestions, and semantic memory uses user interests to expand searches.
entries.aidatatools-dev/astro-agents-mcp: This project provides an MCP endpoint for Western and Vedic astrology at astro-agent.dev/mcp, with no authentication required. Results are deterministic and SHA-256 verifiable, with per-call REST payments available via x402 or MPP.
entries.cablate/Agentic-MCP-Skill: Agentic-MCP-Skill is a progressive MCP client that uses three-layer lazy loading to minimize token usage, with server metadata and tool schemas discovered incrementally. Its socket-based daemon architecture supports persistent connections, making it a fit for Hermes Agent users who want MCP resources loaded progressively.

entries.numtide/llm-agents.nix: This Nix project packages AI coding agents and development tools, including Hermes, and automatically updates its packages daily. Its README provides `nix run` commands for the listed tools, making it a Nix-based option for running Hermes.
entries.marshallrichards/ClawPhone: ClawPhone collects scripts and notes for running agent CLIs, including Hermes Agent, on Android through Termux. It also documents OpenClaw setup and access to device hardware and UI through Termux:API and Termux:GUI.
entries.AbuZar-Ansarii/Hermes-Agent-On-Android: This project provides a Termux installer and guide for running Hermes Agent on Android, using proot-distro Ubuntu. It supports interactive model setup, gateway services, shell commands, and external providers or local models through Ollama.
entries.ultraworkers/hermes-agent-helm-chart: This unofficial community Helm chart deploys Hermes Agent on Kubernetes, with single-writer safeguards for persistent HERMES_HOME storage. It offers direct and CRD-based deployment workflows, plus configurable gateway mode with optional API and webhook listeners.
entries.amirghm/hermes-agent-mobile: This one-command installer brings the Hermes AI assistant to Android through Termux and to iOS through iSH. It also supports Telegram voice and file messaging, and scheduled tasks via cron jobs on Termux.
entries.TheAiSingularity/hermesclaw: hermesclaw runs Hermes Agent with hardware-enforced sandboxing through NVIDIA OpenShell. It restricts network and filesystem access at the kernel level and provides configurable policies for messaging and web search.
entries.solomon2773/nora: Nora is a self-hosted control plane for deploying, monitoring, and operating OpenClaw and Hermes agents on Docker or Kubernetes. It provides searchable logs, metrics, and alert rules, with access through a REST API, CLI, and MCP server.
entries.xmbshwll/hermes-agent-docker: This project provides a Docker sandbox image with mini-swe-agent and the official Hermes installation. It supports persistent state through mounted home directories and lets users build specific Hermes tags with build arguments.
entries.0xrsydn/nix-hermes-agent: This Nix package and NixOS module supports declarative Hermes deployment, including configuration for cli-config.yaml and workspace documents. It combines Nix-managed and CLI-installed skills and supports secrets integration through systemd EnvironmentFiles and sops-nix.
entries.jpalmae/hermeshq: HermesHQ is a Docker-first web control plane for operating multiple Hermes Agent instances, each with separate workspaces and identities. It provides per-agent Telegram and WhatsApp channels and granular tool, path, and network permission policies.
entries.MilkyWay008/Hermes-OTG: Hermes-OTG is a portable Hermes Agent package that runs from a USB drive or other drive without host installation or registry writes. It includes Desktop, TUI, and Gateway modes with isolated data environments, and bundles tools for offline use.
entries.JackTheGit/hermes-autonomous-server: This project sets up Hermes Gateway as a headless, reboot-safe systemd service on Ubuntu and Debian servers. It also supports autonomous execution of recurring AI cron jobs.
entries.jyje/hermes-agent-helm: This project provides a Helm chart for running Hermes Agent on Kubernetes, with installation options via an OCI registry or a published Helm repository. Provider-specific values examples and CI installation on an ephemeral kind cluster make it a deployment option with documented configuration examples and a Kubernetes install check.

entries.TauricResearch/TradingAgents: TradingAgents is a financial trading framework that assigns trading tasks to agents in specialized roles and has them discuss strategies dynamically. It is designed for research purposes.
entries.builderz-labs/mission-control: Mission Control is a self-hosted system for governing agent tasks, registrations, memory browsing, and cost tracking. It stands out for offering Web UI, CLI, MCP server, and REST API interfaces, with local Node.js installation or Docker deployment.
entries.agent-of-empires/agent-of-empires: Agent of Empires provides a TUI and web control surface for managing multiple coding agents, including Hermes Agent. It supports persistent tmux sessions, Git worktrees, and multi-repository workspaces, with a web dashboard for structured views, terminal access, and diffs.
entries.shannhk/hermes-agent-control-room: Hermes Agent Control Room is a template for scaling Hermes Agent from a single VPS agent to specialist teams and automated workflows. Its level-based architecture and task bus support delegation and handoffs, and it includes skills for VPS provisioning, security auditing, and backup management.
entries.swarmclawai/swarmclaw: SwarmClaw is a framework for building autonomous agent swarms, with support for 23+ LLM providers, durable agent memory, and MCP tool integration. Visual org charts provide a way to represent team delegation.
entries.agent37-platform/minions: Minions is a control interface for creating, supervising, and reviewing autonomous Hermes Agent work. It combines a Kanban board and live streams of agent reasoning and tool execution with human verification of agent-proposed task completions.
entries.1ilkhamov/opencode-hermes-multiagent: This project coordinates 17 specialized agents across research, planning, implementation, quality, and infrastructure. A strict pipeline architecture and Master Orchestrator handle routing and coordination.
entries.linke-ai/hermes-agent-team: Hermes Agent Team is a local web system for coordinating Leader and Specialist agents through an automated task lifecycle. It integrates MCP and ACP for local tools and communication, with a real-time UI for agent dialogues and Kanban task flows.
entries.howdymary/hermes-agent-metaharness: Hermes Agent Metaharness automates outer-loop optimization of benchmark harness code and orchestrates TBLite and TerminalBench-2 evaluations. It also provides structured candidate mutation and frontier tracking.
entries.runtimenoteslabs/gladiator: Gladiator runs an agent-versus-agent arena in which nine autonomous agents operate across two competing AI companies. Using Paperclip and Hermes Agent for task execution and learning, it displays agent tasks, code, and scoreboard metrics on a real-time dashboard.
entries.InfiniteWhispers/HermesAgent-MultiModel: HermesAgent-MultiModel is a local Mixture-of-Agents framework that queries models in parallel and synthesizes their outputs, using Hermes for task routing and tool-calling. It is designed for consumer GPUs, is optimized for RTX 4080/5080 hardware, and does not require cloud dependencies.

entries.colbymchenry/codegraph: Codegraph builds a local, pre-indexed project graph with `codegraph init` and automatically syncs it when files change. Its MCP server connects that graph to Hermes Agent and other coding agents, providing project knowledge intended to reduce token usage and tool calls.
entries.junhoyeo/tokscale: Tokscale tracks token usage across AI coding agents, including Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini. Its visualization dashboard helps users analyze usage across those clients.
entries.liaohch3/claude-tap: Claude Tap is a local trace viewer for coding-agent API traffic, including traffic from Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and OpenCode. It displays prompts, tool calls, streaming responses, and token usage; users can compare adjacent requests and redact common auth headers before recording traces.
entries.Javis603/token-monitor: Token Monitor provides a real-time widget for token usage, costs, and rate limits, reading Hermes Agent state alongside other CLI tools. It supports 46+ AI coding tools and adds historical trends, usage breakdowns, and multi-device sync.
entries.bergside/typeui: TypeUI provides design skills, UI prompts, and layout guidance for building interfaces with AI. It supports providers that accept Markdown or general prompting and connects to coding tools through TypeUI MCP or plugins.
entries.Salomondiei08/oh-my-hermes: Oh My Hermes is an installable workflow layer for building, shipping, and operating apps with Hermes Agent. It includes product development and operations skills, plus a CTO loop with seven focused agents.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-skins: Hermes Skins is a community CLI for skins and themes for the Hermes terminal UI, with listings for custom and built-in skins. Users can create skins with YAML files, and custom skins inherit unspecified values from the default skin.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/lintlang: Lintlang statically checks agent configs, tool descriptions, and system prompts, with HERM v1.1 scoring. It scans agent-facing content in project directories and reports file locations and suggested fixes, with support for CI gates and reviewed baselines.
entries.tinyhumansai/tiny.place: Tiny.place is a social economy for autonomous AI agents, with identity registration through human-readable @handles and encrypted agent-to-agent messaging via Signal Protocol. It also supports commerce through Solana-based USDC and SOL payments.
entries.unmodeled-tyler/vessel-browser: Vessel Browser is an AI-native browser built for autonomous agent control via MCP. It supports external MCP clients and browser automation workflows, with a supervisor sidebar for agent approvals, checkpoints, and conversation threads.
entries.AlexAI-MCP/hermes-CCC: Hermes-CCC ports the Hermes Agent brain and 46 core skills to Claude Code Channel. It runs natively in Claude Code without separate processes or OAuth and includes MLOps tools for vLLM, GGUF inference, and RL training.
entries.topoteretes/cognee-integrations: Cognee Integrations is a monorepo of Cognee-owned integration packages organized around two tiers: a permanent knowledge graph and a session cache. Its Claude Code plugin automatically captures and recalls context.
entries.adityahimaone/hermes-agent-rtk-caveman: This setup combines RTK and Caveman templating for token-saving CLI workflows, with a stated 90–99% token savings. It includes 40+ preconfigured skills for finance, DevOps, and research, plus automated installation for macOS and Linux.
entries.Abruptive/Ankh.md: Ankh.md is a framework for creating Hermes agents scoped to individual folders, with local configuration and skills. It can switch between the default and scoped agents and supports project-local memories, tools, and custom instructions.
entries.42-evey/evey-setup: evey-setup automates installation of Hermes Agent and 12+ supporting services, with three deployment tiers ranging from a minimum viable setup to a production stack. It also supports 29 community plugins across six functional categories.
entries.0xNyk/openclaw-to-hermes: This tool migrates OpenClaw data—including SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, skills, and memory archives—to Hermes. It also maps configurations and credentials to Hermes YAML and JSON formats and can set up systemd gateway services.
entries.observeco/observeco: Observeco is a Hermes plugin that exports real-time telemetry from agent conversations for monitoring and recovery of multi-agent systems. It offers passive analysis without token use and scheduled active probing, and its config-aware baselines detect performance drift relative to local file changes.
entries.handnewb/hermes-voice: hermes-voice adds voice interaction to Hermes Agent, with support for 35 languages via Piper and 9 via Kokoro. It runs offline without API keys or accounts and includes adaptive turn-taking and barge-in.
entries.33hodl/hermes-startup: hermes-startup is a local runtime for using Hermes Agent to pursue online earnings opportunities, operating in deterministic zero-network mode by default. It requires explicit approval for consequential actions and external writes, and includes contracts for opportunities, offer previews, and exact approvals.
entries.181079342/hermes-memoss: hermes-memoss is a MemOS memory plugin that supports semantic search and multi-dimensional memory storage. It provides tools to search, add, and delete memories, with a circuit breaker for MemOS API outages.

entries.farion1231/cc-switch: CC Switch is a cross-platform manager for Hermes Agent and several other agent tools, including Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, and Gemini CLI. It lets users switch API providers in one click and manage MCP, Skills, and Prompts in one place, with support for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
entries.iOfficeAI/AionUi: AionUi is a local open-source cowork app for Hermes Agent and other agent CLIs, with a built-in agent that does not require a separate CLI installation. It also includes 21 professional assistants and supports macOS, Windows, and Linux.
entries.nesquena/hermes-webui: Hermes WebUI provides a three-panel interface for sessions, chat, and workspace files, with controls for profiles, models, and workspaces. Built with Python and vanilla JavaScript, it requires no build step and is designed for using Hermes Agent from the web or a phone.
entries.fathah/hermes-desktop: Hermes Desktop is a desktop companion for installing, configuring, and chatting with Hermes Agent, using the official Hermes install script. Its GUI manages profiles, sessions, skills, and tools, and the app is available from the project website or GitHub Releases.
entries.EKKOLearnAI/ekko-studio: Ekko Studio is a web dashboard for Hermes Agent that brings together chats, sessions, agent integrations, scheduled jobs, usage analytics, and channel configuration. It also supports visual workflows with schedules and approval gates, and is available as a desktop app, npm CLI, or Docker image.
entries.outsourc-e/hermes-workspace: Hermes Workspace is a web workspace combining chat, a terminal, a memory browser, a skills manager, and an inspector panel. Its highlights include Swarm Mode with role-based dispatch and tmux-backed workers, plus a file browser with Monaco and a PTY terminal.
entries.spacering-net/codeg: Codeg is a collaborative coding workspace that aggregates sessions from Hermes and other agents, including Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode, as a desktop or self-hosted app. Users can import, search, resume, and hand off sessions, delegate across agents, or queue to-dos in worktrees.
entries.dodo-reach/hermes-desktop: This native Mac workspace connects directly to Hermes hosts locally or over SSH and presents sessions, Kanban, skills, and cron jobs in dedicated views. Its embedded terminal provides direct shell access, including for system repair.
entries.Eynzof/Hermes-CN-Desktop: Hermes-CN-Desktop is a Windows-first desktop app for Hermes Agent, supporting Windows and macOS with native window and process management. It includes a built-in Hermes-CN-Core kernel with health checks and updates, alongside chat, memory management, and LaTeX and Markdown rendering.
entries.abundantbeing/hermes-browser-extension: This Chromium side-panel extension connects the active browser context to a local, Hermes Cloud, or self-hosted remote Hermes Agent runtime. It offers Bot Mode for agent switching and group chats; Hermes Control is opt-in and Chromium-only.
entries.uzairansaruzi/hermex: Hermex is a native SwiftUI iPhone app for driving a self-hosted Hermes agent by pairing with a hermes-webui server. It supports streaming chats with file or image attachments and lets users browse, search, and resume sessions, as well as view scheduled tasks, skills, memory, and insights.
entries.freestylefly/wesight: Wesight is a desktop AI agent workspace with one-click setup for Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw, along with custom LLM model routing. Its runtime dashboard tracks token usage and latency, while a live workspace shows code writes and diffs.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is an interactive TUI with nine tabs and four selectable color themes for monitoring Hermes. It tracks agent growth, Git projects, and scheduled cron jobs, and provides a tmux operator view for managing live agent panes.
entries.jazzyalex/agent-sessions: This native macOS app brings together session browsing, analytics, and quota tracking for Hermes agents and other coding-agent CLIs. It searches prompts, tool activity, errors, and file paths, tracks Codex and Claude quota burn per session, and builds its search index locally.
entries.xaspx/hermes-control-interface: This self-hosted web dashboard provides a browser-based interface to the Hermes AI agent stack, including a terminal, file explorer, session overview, cron management, system metrics, and agent status panel. Its highlights also include real-time chat with tool-call visualization, MCP server lifecycle controls, and a ZOO Swarm Monitor for agent health and kanban pipelines.
entries.nickvasilescu/hermes-desktop-os1: This native macOS workspace runs Hermes Agent on Orgo cloud computers and SSH hosts. It offers one-click automated installation on fresh cloud computers and integrated WebRTC voice mode using OpenAI Realtime and Orgo MCP.
entries.sharbelxyz/hermes-agent-mission-control: This self-hostable mission-control dashboard template connects a local Hermes agent to web dashboards through a Postgres message bus. Its approval inbox lets users review requests with side effects before they proceed.
entries.liftaris/herm: Herm is an alternative Hermes TUI and dashboard built with OpenTUI for chatting and managing agent sessions. It also includes a kanban board for agentic work and tools for managing profiles, skills, cron jobs, and toolsets.
entries.clawvader-tech/hermes-telegram-miniapp: This locally run React SPA is a 10-page, mobile-first dashboard for Telegram Mini App v2.0. It combines terminal chat with streaming responses and file attachments, Telegram validation using dual HMAC-SHA256 and Ed25519 authentication, and background agent spawning for up to five concurrent instances.
entries.aivrar/portable-hermes-agent: This project packages Hermes Agent as a portable Windows desktop app with a dark-themed, multilingual GUI and session management. It supports local models through LM Studio and includes workflow automation and runtime tool creation.
entries.pyrate-llama/hermes-ui: Hermes UI is a self-hosted assistant interface with a glassmorphic design, chat, and real-time log streaming. It also provides a file browser, task tracking dashboard, and management tools for skills, cron jobs, and MCP servers.
entries.sanchomuzax/hermes-webui: This dashboard focuses on monitoring Hermes processes and configuring the system. It shows session activity and costs in real time, supports inspection of conversation histories and skill source code, and provides read-only views of configuration and environment variables.
entries.Euraika-Labs/pan-ui: Pan-UI is a self-hosted, chat-first AI workspace with real-time SSE streaming and tool approval cards. Its marketplace supports discovering and installing skills and MCP servers, while isolated profiles keep sessions, memory, and API keys separate.
entries.Felix-Forever/hermes-agent-desktop: This native desktop client centers on multi-agent collaboration, with 20 specialized AI agents and a PM orchestrator. It also offers a visual Skill Store with 50+ curated one-click installations, streaming SSE responses, and model switching.
entries.nicolasestrem/hermes-model-switcher: This plugin displays configured model routes across Hermes Agent profiles in one matrix and lets you preview changes before applying them. Named presets and guarded Undo make it a focused option for switching models from the Hermes Agent Web Dashboard.
entries.robbyczgw-cla/hermes-ui-plus: This unofficial, open-source chat client for self-hosted Hermes Agent supports interactive answers such as checklists, choices, forms, rankings, and votes. It also provides command approvals and live tool-step updates, with clients for Android, web, and macOS plus a Linux alpha.
